bridges.title: The Same Fall, Closer
bridges.text: Kings tells the destruction of Jerusalem from a distance, in a few verses. The next seven chapters are the same catastrophe told from inside the walls, by a prophet who lived through the siege.

bridges.title: Two Exiles
bridges.text: The story now steps back a century and a half. When Assyria destroyed the northern kingdom in 722 BC, its people were deported to Nineveh; Tobit is their story. Daniel follows the later exiles of Judah to Babylon.

bridges.title: From Persia to the Greeks
bridges.text: Nehemiah ends around 430 BC in a small Persian province. A century later Alexander the Great conquered Persia, and Judea passed to his successors: first the Ptolemies of Egypt, then, from about 200 BC, the Seleucids of Syria. In Alexandria, Jewish scholars translated the Scriptures into Greek, the Septuagint, which the early church would read. 1 Maccabees opens with Alexander and moves quickly to the crisis of 167 BC.

bridges.title: The Road to Bethlehem
bridges.text: Simon's heirs, the Hasmoneans, ruled an independent Jewish state for about eighty years. In this era the Pharisees and Sadducees took shape, synagogues spread, and the community behind the Dead Sea Scrolls withdrew to the desert. Rome's general Pompey took Jerusalem in 63 BC. Rome later made Herod king of Judea; he rebuilt the temple on a grand scale. Luke opens in Herod's last years.
